prompts.concept: Neighbor-Joining starts from the distance matrix. Which two taxa join first? Pick a cell in the matrix, or click two leaves in a tree.
prompts.math: NJ joins the pair minimizing Q(i,j) = (n−2)·d(i,j) − R_i − R_j. Use the Distance/Q switch to see Q directly — the smallest off-diagonal value wins.

prompts.concept: Four clusters remain: u1, u2, E and F. Which pair joins next? The tempting answer is the closest pair — is it?
prompts.math: Q(i,j) = (n−2)·d(i,j) − R_i − R_j subtracts each cluster's average divergence. A pair close to each other can still lose to a pair whose members are far from everything else.
prompts.reveal: u1 and u2 are closest, but NJ joins E and F: they are close relative to how far each is from everything else.

prompts.concept: The tree is complete: RF = 0, so every grouping in the true tree was recovered.
prompts.math: RF counts splits present in one tree but not the other. Two unrooted 6-taxon trees can differ on at most 2·(6−3) = 6 splits.
